facts_and_goals: A trusted former colleague offered to review my portfolio for free next week. They work in the field I hope to enter, and no confidential work is included. I can choose which suggestions to use. I want to improve the portfolio but worry that criticism will be uncomfortable.

relevant_considerations.text: Feedback matches the goal and does not require accepting every suggestion.
Discomfort is different from evidence the review is harmful.
Agree on the kind of feedback desired.

facts_and_goals: Someone I barely know asked me to do a large unpaid project with an unspecified deadline. They said it might lead to exposure, but cannot explain who will see it. I already have paid deadlines and want to build experience without missing them.
option_a: commit to the entire unpaid project now
option_b: decline or request a smaller clearly defined scope first

relevant_considerations.text: The scope and expected benefit are unclear.
Existing paid deadlines could be affected.
A bounded trial is different from an open-ended commitment.

facts_and_goals: I can work at either of two company offices with the same role, pay, and commute time. One has my close colleagues; the other has people from a team I might collaborate with later. I value both familiar support and new connections. I can visit each before deciding.
option_a: choose the office with the new team
option_b: choose the office with familiar colleagues

relevant_considerations.text: Both options fit the practical constraints.
Familiar support and new connections both match stated values.
Visits could provide information without an immediate commitment.

facts_and_goals: My instructor offers a short consultation on essay outlines before drafting. I have an outline and an appointment is available during a free period. The consultation is optional and not graded. I want to identify weaknesses early, though I feel awkward asking for feedback.

relevant_considerations.text: Early feedback could reveal problems before a full draft.
The appointment fits the schedule and is not graded.
Prepare specific questions to make the short session useful.

facts_and_goals: I am already struggling with my required courses and have missed two assignments. An extra optional course sounds interesting but is offered again next term. Adding it is not necessary for graduation. I want to learn it well without falling further behind.
option_a: add the extra course this term

relevant_considerations.text: Current workload is already causing missed work.
Waiting does not block graduation.
Interest does not remove the time constraint.

facts_and_goals: For a class project, I can study a familiar topic in depth or learn a new topic from scratch. The instructor says both can meet the rubric. I have enough time for either and enjoy both depth and exploration. I have not yet sketched what each project would involve.

relevant_considerations.text: Both options can meet the rubric.
Scope a small outline for each before comparing.
Depth and exploration are both legitimate priorities.

facts_and_goals: I interrupted a friend repeatedly during dinner and they told me afterward that it bothered them. I remember doing it and have not apologized. They are willing to talk privately. I want to repair the interaction without making it about defending myself.
option_b: wait and hope the issue passes

relevant_considerations.text: The friend directly explained the concern.
A specific apology can acknowledge the behavior.
Avoid assuming what response the friend will give.

facts_and_goals: I heard secondhand that a friend criticized me, but I have not seen the message or asked them about it. I am considering accusing them in a group chat. We usually communicate respectfully. I want clarity without creating an unnecessary public conflict.
option_a: post the accusation in the group chat
option_b: ask the friend privately what happened first

relevant_considerations.text: The information is secondhand and incomplete.
A public accusation may escalate the conflict.
A private question better tests the interpretation.

facts_and_goals: A relative wants to stay with me for a weekend. We get along, but I also need quiet time after a busy week. There is no emergency, and they would accept a shorter visit. I want to maintain the relationship and protect my time.

relevant_considerations.text: Both relationship and rest are stated priorities.
A shorter visit is an available compromise.
Clarify expectations rather than infer disappointment.

facts_and_goals: My old phone occasionally shuts down, and it holds the only copies of family photos. I have a private external drive with enough space and time to copy the photos today without deleting the originals. I want to preserve them but keep putting off the task because it feels tedious.
option_a: make and check a backup copy of the photos
option_b: continue relying on the phone as the only copy

relevant_considerations.text: The phone is currently the only copy and has reliability problems.
A second copy can be made without deleting the originals.
Verify that the copied photos open correctly.

facts_and_goals: I rent a storage unit that holds only empty boxes and furniture I have not used in years. It costs money each month and I can cancel after clearing it. I have time this weekend to sort it, though the task feels tedious. I want to lower recurring expenses.
option_a: keep renewing the storage unit without sorting it
option_b: sort it and decide what to keep before the next renewal

relevant_considerations.text: The recurring cost conflicts with the stated goal.
The stored items may have limited current use.
Sorting need not mean discarding everything.

facts_and_goals: I have a free Saturday and can either take a nearby day trip or spend it at home on hobbies. Both fit my budget and neither affects obligations. I have enjoyed both recently. I want a restorative day but am unsure whether novelty or quiet would help more.

relevant_considerations.text: Both choices fit the practical constraints.
Restoration depends on the kind of rest desired.
A shorter outing or flexible plan may combine benefits.
